caveats: **A clean scan is not "patched".** CVE matching uses a fixed, built-in table of 41 rules over 21 product names, and nothing outside it is reported: other products, CVEs after 2024, operating-system patches, kernels and distribution back-ports. Software the leg cannot list (other accounts' per-user installs on Windows, any host with none of the four Linux package managers) is not examined. On macOS, Homebrew formulae and casks are never matched, so a clean macOS result is not evidence about them; use pkg_inventory.packages (which lists, not matches). `cve_scan` and `scan` end with an `INFO|scan|Coverage|...` row and `summary` with `summary|COVERAGE|...`, in the same output as the `CONSTRAINED` result status; `inventory` returns software rows only. The status itself reaches the agent log, not REST, MCP or the dashboard, so the in-band row is what an operator sees.

**Substring matching produces false positives, and the version test is naive.** A rule fires on any installed name that contains its product text, so `python` matches `python3-wheel`, `git` matches `git-man`, and `windows` matches .NET runtimes and Windows utilities; the version is compared as dotted numbers, and a Debian epoch such as `1:2.47.3` is compared as text and reads as lower than `2.45.1`. The samples show all three, so some `cve` rows are not exposures, and the issue count in `summary` is inflated by them.

**A failed read usually becomes the check's default result, not an error.** Windows registry reads fall back to a default (a missing SMBv1 value reads as enabled; an unreadable UAC or firewall value reads as disabled), a failed Linux command returns empty output, and only the Linux file checks and the macOS status tools surface `UNREADABLE`. No capture observed a real permission denial, so this is read from the code, not measured; the World-Writable PATH walk also skips an entry whose `stat()` fails (#5515).

**`summary` does not match its declared result columns.** It emits three pipe fields per row (`summary|<severity or TOTAL>|<count>`) against two declared columns, `severity` and `count`, and the `TOTAL` row's `count` cell is the string `<n> findings (<n> issues)` rather than the declared `int32`.

**Configuration checks are single-signal heuristics, not effective policy.** On macOS the six tools' expected output lines were verified on macOS 27.0.1 only (exit codes not captured; 13 to 15 not measured), so a Mac whose tool prints something else reports `UNREADABLE`, not a verdict. Each reads one registry value, one command's text or one file, so a setting applied another way (an `Include`d SSH file, a managed firewall, a third-party antivirus) can read differently from the host's real state. There is no `docs/agent-privilege-model.md` row for this plugin, so the Privileges table records only what each capture measured.

definitions.description: Run security configuration compliance checks on the endpoint. Verifies settings such as firewall state, password policy, remote desktop configuration, and other hardening baselines. Returns findings classified by severity. Does not include CVE matching; use the full "scan" action for combined results. On macOS a check whose system tool could not be read (missing, failed, no permission, unrecognised output) is reported as an UNREADABLE row with detail "Unknown (read failed)" and severity UNREADABLE, never as a finding.

Scan installed software against known CVE rules. Enumerates installed applications (registry on Windows, dpkg/rpm/pacman on Linux, system_profiler on macOS; Homebrew formulae and casks are not scanned, use pkg_inventory.packages) and compares versions against the built-in CVE database. Returns only CVE findings, not configuration checks. A result with no CVE rows means only that no built-in rule matched the software enumerated above; on macOS the run ends with an INFO row titled "Coverage" saying so, or an UNREADABLE Coverage row (and no "No vulnerabilities" row) when system_profiler could not be read completely. Use the full "scan" action for combined results.

Return the raw installed software inventory (name and version pairs) for server-side NVD matching. This is a lightweight alternative to client-side CVE scanning that enables the server to perform centralized vulnerability correlation against the full NVD database. On macOS the list is system_profiler applications only; Homebrew formulae and casks are not included (use pkg_inventory.packages), and a macOS run that read nothing returns no rows. The rows are pure name|version pairs with no coverage row, and the coverage status is visible only in the agent log (not in REST, MCP or the dashboard): treat the list as "system_profiler applications only, Homebrew excluded", and never read an empty macOS list as "no software installed".

Run a full host vulnerability scan combining CVE matching and configuration compliance checks. CVE matching compares installed software versions against a built-in rule database. Configuration checks verify security hardening settings (firewall state, password policy, remote desktop config, etc.). Each finding is classified by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO, or UNREADABLE when the check could not run; not an issue). On macOS, Homebrew formulae and casks are not scanned (use pkg_inventory.packages); the run ends with a row titled "Coverage" saying so (INFO, or UNREADABLE when the software list or a configuration read failed), and a result with no CVE rows means only that no built-in rule matched the software enumerated. Reports progress at 0%, 50%, 90%, 100%.

Run a full vulnerability scan (CVE + configuration) and return only the severity summary counts. Provides a quick overview of the endpoint's security posture without the full finding details. Returns total findings, total issues, and per-severity counts (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO, UNREADABLE; UNREADABLE means the check could not run and is not counted as an issue). On macOS, Homebrew formulae and casks are not scanned (use pkg_inventory.packages), and the output ends with summary|COVERAGE|<text> rows saying so (one per cause); the counts cover only the software enumerated.

description: Host vulnerability scanning — CVE matching and configuration compliance checks
how_it_works:
Every action is a read; nothing on the host is changed. `scan` first reads the installed-software list and matches it against a fixed table of 41 built-in CVE rules, then runs the fixed list of configuration checks for the operating system, and returns the CVE rows followed by the configuration rows (progress is reported at 0, 50, 90 and 100). `cve_scan` and `config_scan` are those two halves on their own. `summary` runs the same combined scan, throws the individual rows away and returns only a count per severity. `inventory` runs neither scan: it returns the raw installed-software `name|version` pairs and nothing else.

The CVE half is deliberately small and local. It is not a vulnerability feed: the rule table ships inside the plugin, each rule names a product by a short text (for example `openssl` or `git`), and a rule fires when an installed product's name contains that text, ignoring case, and its version compares lower than the rule's fixed version. The configuration half reads a handful of well-known hardening settings (registry values on Windows, command output and a few files on macOS and Linux) and reports every check it ran, passing ones as `INFO`. `inventory` exists so a caller can hand the raw software list to the server for a fuller match instead of relying on the built-in table.

### What you can decide with it

| Question | Action | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Which known-bad versions of a short list of common products are installed? | `cve_scan` | Windows: from the registry Uninstall lists (machine-wide, 32-bit, and the agent account's own). macOS: apps from `system_profiler` only; Homebrew formulae and casks are not scanned (see `pkg_inventory.packages`). Linux: packages from the first package manager found (`dpkg-query`, else `rpm`, else `pacman`, else `apk`). |
| Is this host's basic hardening in place? | `config_scan` | A fixed per-OS list of checks, listed below. Every check that ran is reported, passing ones as `INFO`. |
| Both of the above in one call | `scan` | CVE rows, then configuration rows. |
| How bad is it at a glance? | `summary` | `TOTAL` first, then a count for each of `CRITICAL`, `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`, `INFO`, `UNREADABLE`. `UNREADABLE` and `INFO` are not issues. On macOS the output ends with one `summary\|COVERAGE\|<text>` row per coverage cause (see Result status). |
| What software is installed, for matching elsewhere? | `inventory` | Raw `name\|version` pairs. No CVE or configuration logic. |

**What a clean result means.** A scan with no `cve` rows says only that none of the 41 built-in rules matched the installed software. It does not say the host is patched. The table covers 21 product names (OpenSSL, curl, sudo, polkit, Log4j, Apache, OpenSSH, Python, Node.js, Chrome, Firefox, .NET, OpenJDK, Windows, nginx, PostgreSQL, Git, 7-Zip, WinRAR, PuTTY, PHP) with one to four rules each, and no rule is for a CVE newer than 2024. Software that is not in the software list the leg reads (per-user installs of other accounts on Windows, anything on Linux when none of the four package managers is present) is never examined. Operating-system patch level, kernel, firmware and distribution back-ports are not assessed at all. For a real patch-compliance answer use a patch-state source, not this plugin.

**What a `cve` row means.** It is a lead to check, not a confirmed exposure. Matching is by substring of the product name and by a simple dotted-number version comparison, so some rows are false positives (see Caveat 2). The two Windows Print Spooler rules in particular compare an application's own version against a Windows build number and never read the real OS build or installed hotfixes, so they cannot tell you whether PrintNightmare is fixed; in the Windows sample every Print Spooler row names a .NET runtime, a Windows update package or a Windows utility, not the spooler itself.

**Configuration checks by OS** (severity is fixed per check; a passing check is `INFO`):

| OS | Checks that always report | Checks that report only in some cases | Known ways the answer can be wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows | UAC (`EnableLUA`), SMBv1 (`SMB1`), Auto-Logon, Defender real-time flag (`DisableRealtimeMonitoring`), Firewall for the Domain, Private and Public profiles | RDP Network Level Authentication, only when Remote Desktop is enabled | A missing SMBv1 value is read as enabled (`CRITICAL`); a missing Defender flag is read as enabled protection; the Defender row is one registry flag, not the live service state; an unreadable UAC or firewall value reads as disabled. |
| macOS | Gatekeeper (`spctl`), FileVault (`fdesetup`), SIP (`csrutil`), Application Firewall (`socketfilterfw`), Remote Login (`systemsetup`), Automatic Software Updates (`defaults`) | none | A verdict needs the tool to have run to a clean exit 0 and its first output line to EQUAL the expected text (for example `FileVault is On.`, `assessments enabled`, `System Integrity Protection status: enabled.`, `Firewall is enabled. (State = 1)`, `Remote Login: Off`, `1`); anything else (a missing tool, a refused call, a localized message, `enabled (Custom Configuration).`) is an `UNREADABLE` row with detail `Unknown (read failed)`, never a finding and never a pass. The expected lines were verified on macOS 27.0.1 (one Apple Silicon host); macOS 13 to 15 were not measured, and no tool's exit code has been captured, so exit 0 is still required for every verdict. On a default install `defaults read ... AutomaticCheckEnabled` prints `Error: Could not find key 'AutomaticCheckEnabled' in domain 'com.apple.SoftwareUpdate'.`: an absent key is reported as `INFO` "Automatic update check: not set (macOS default applies)", not as unreadable and not as a finding (`0` is the disabled value). The risky-port check is not expected to produce rows: the plugin runs `ss -tlnH || netstat -tlnp` and discards errors, and `ss` is not present on macOS and `netstat -tlnp` is believed not to be valid there (inferred, not captured). |
| Linux | ASLR (`randomize_va_space`), SUID core dumps (`suid_dumpable`), SSH Root Login, Firewall | SSH Password Authentication, only if `sshd_config` sets it (it also reports `INFO` "not applicable" when the file is absent and `UNREADABLE` when it cannot be read); `/tmp noexec`, only if `/tmp` is a separate mount; World-Writable PATH, only if the agent's own `PATH` has such a directory; Open Port rows for FTP 21, Telnet 23, SMB 445, RDP 3389, VNC 5900 bound on all interfaces | Only `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` is read (no `Include`d files, no `Match` blocks, no effective-config query); a plain `PermitRootLogin prohibit-password` reads as "not explicitly set". The firewall check reads `iptables`, `nft` and `ufw` output, which normally need root, so an unprivileged agent reports `No firewall rules detected` (`HIGH`) even on a protected host. |

A Linux file the agent cannot read (SSH config, ASLR, `suid_dumpable`, the mount table) is reported as `UNREADABLE`, never as a weak setting. An absent `sshd_config` is `INFO`, "not applicable".

### Diagrams

The CVE branch and the configuration branch are independent: neither can suppress the other, and `scan` simply concatenates them. A software entry with no version is skipped, so it can never match. The last two configuration branches are the important difference: a failed Linux file read is surfaced as `UNREADABLE`, while a failed registry or command read silently falls through to that check's default result.

`summary` counts rows, not distinct problems. One installed product that matches two rules, or several installed products that match one rule, each add to the issue count, so the number is an upper bound on real exposures and is inflated by false-positive `cve` rows.

outputs_note:
Pipe-delimited rows, one per finding (or per installed package for `inventory`). `scan`, `cve_scan` and `config_scan` share the 4-field row shape `severity|category|title|detail`. An action that finds nothing still emits one placeholder row, `INFO|scan|No vulnerabilities|No issues detected`; in practice only `cve_scan` reaches it, because `config_scan` and `scan` always report at least one configuration check. `summary` emits a different, 3-field shape: a literal `summary` discriminator, then a severity name (or the literal `TOTAL`), then a count, which is one field more than the two result columns (`severity`, `count`) the definition declares. `inventory` emits raw `name|version` pairs with no discriminator, and `version` is empty when the source gives none.

A Linux config check whose file read fails (EACCES, EIO, ...) emits `UNREADABLE|config|<title>|<path>: <cause>` (for example `eacces`) rather than a finding about an empty value. `UNREADABLE` means the check could not run; it is not an issue, so `summary` leaves it out of the `TOTAL` row's issue count and reports it on its own `summary|UNREADABLE|<n>` row after `summary|INFO|<n>`. An absent `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` is not a weak setting: both SSH checks emit `INFO` with "/etc/ssh/sshd_config not present; check not applicable".

privileges.grant: None established; the plugin reads `HKLM` Uninstall and policy values and the agent account's own `HKCU` Uninstall list. No row in `docs/agent-privilege-model.md`
privileges.if_refused: not observed; a denied `RegOpenKeyExW` or `RegQueryValueExW` returns an empty string or the check's default, so a blocked read shows up as that check's default result, not an error

privileges.grant: `systemsetup -getremotelogin` needs administrator rights (root has them). No other grant. No row for this plugin
privileges.if_refused: not observed for a denial; a refused or failed tool is an `UNREADABLE` row with detail `Unknown (read failed)` (Remote Login included), not a finding
privileges.measured: 2026-09-07, bare metal, as an unprivileged user (euid 501), not as root
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon; the shipped LaunchDaemon runs as root today (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

privileges.grant: None for the package list, `/proc` or world-readable files. `iptables`, `nft` and `ufw status` normally need root or `CAP_NET_ADMIN`; a mode-0600 `sshd_config` (the RHEL-family default) needs read access. No row for this plugin
privileges.if_refused: a failed file read is `UNREADABLE` (both SSH checks on a 0600 `sshd_config`); a failed firewall command returns empty output, read as "no firewall rules detected"
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, dedicated unprivileged account by design (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

result_status.when: every action on Windows and Linux, and macOS `config_scan` when every check read cleanly: the plugin does not set a typed result status, so a consumer must read the rows. A failed read is therefore never visible in the status; it shows only as an `UNREADABLE` row (Linux file checks) or as a default-branch finding

macOS `cve_scan`, `scan`, `summary` and `inventory` when `system_profiler` returned applications. `cve_scan` and `scan` also emit `INFO|scan|Coverage|Homebrew formulae and casks are not scanned`, and `summary` emits `summary|COVERAGE|<same text>`; `inventory` emits no such row. Homebrew formulae and casks are never read, so a result with no CVE rows means only that no built-in rule matched the applications `system_profiler` listed

the same four macOS actions when the `system_profiler` command failed to run, exited non-zero, or returned no applications. No application is returned to CVE matching or `inventory` from a run that did not finish cleanly (a partial list could read a truncated version as vulnerable or hide a real one). `cve_scan` and `scan` suppress the "No vulnerabilities" placeholder and end with `UNREADABLE|scan|Coverage|<text>`, `summary` with `summary|COVERAGE|<text>`, and `inventory` is empty. The text reads "The macOS software list could not be read completely (system_profiler failed, timed out, exceeded the output cap or returned no applications); not a clean result". The macOS commands run with a 60 s deadline and an 8 MB output cap (the process group is killed at the deadline); either one counts as unreadable

macOS `config_scan`, `scan` and `summary` when a configuration check's system tool could not be read (missing, non-zero exit, no output, permission message, or text that is not the tool's expected line, such as a localized message). That check emits `UNREADABLE|config|<check>|Unknown (read failed)` instead of a finding, counted in `summary`'s `UNREADABLE` bucket, and `config_scan`, `scan` and `summary` add `UNREADABLE|scan|Coverage|One or more macOS configuration checks could not be read; each is reported as an UNREADABLE row, not as a finding` (`summary|COVERAGE|...` for `summary`). The provenance is one token: a software-list token outranks this one, which outranks `homebrew_not_scanned`; the in-band rows list every cause

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result only.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore, rendered by the dashboard and REST with the plugin's default column schema (`Agent, Severity, Category, Title, Detail`) or, when the request carries a definition id, that definition's own result-column schema.

**Server-side NVD matching.** The `inventory` definition says its rows are for server-side NVD matching and centralized correlation; this README does not describe that server feature. The server's version comparison notes that it duplicates the algorithm in `cve_rules.hpp`.
**Not consumed by** daily-sync inventory, Echo, DEX or metrics; nothing runs on a schedule and every action is on-demand.

**Sensitivity.** `cve` rows embed installed application names and versions in `detail`, and `inventory` returns that list directly: an installed-software inventory by another route. Configuration rows reveal the host's security posture (for example a disabled firewall or SMBv1 enabled), which is useful to an attacker as well as an administrator. Nothing in either row shape names a person.

**Siblings:** `installed_apps` is a separate installed-software collector with overlapping data (it shares the "installed, held" package-presence convention on Linux); a caller working from software identity may have two plugins to reconcile.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) then `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) then `discover_instructions` or `get_definition("security.vuln_scan.scan")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`.
